headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks from shared MCP/egress pathways; compliance risk is low but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP surfaces and agent_a can use stdin/stdout plus MCP, while agent_b offers an MCP server. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if agent_a ingests agent_b outputs or shared workspace content as trusted text. No direct proof of a shared channel is provided, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a reads agent_b-produced text from MCP, files, or stdout as instructions
IF both agents are connected through the same MCP broker or shared workspace
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following for any MCP-fed text
Separate MCP endpoints per agent
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require manual review before executing parsed directives
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets (Ed25519 signatures), and agent_b handles long-term user facts and conversational context. Both have allowlisted network egress and MCP access, so a shared workspace or API bridge could leak sensitive data across agents. The exact transport is undocumented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace, API token, or MCP broker
IF agent_a forwards repository content or prompts into agent_b requests
mitigations: Isolate workspaces and credentials per agent
Block secret-bearing files from inter-agent transfer
Turn off automatic context sharing between agents
Review outbound allowlists for both agents
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on MCP/API payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b exposes MCP/API access but no write permissions are documented. A conflict is plausible if both operate on the same repo or mutable resource, but the profiles do not prove overlapping writes by agent_b, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same repository or database
IF agent_b is configured to issue state-changing MCP/API calls through a shared backend
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a lock
Restrict agent_b to read-only calls
Require explicit checkout/commit ownership
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and modify repository artifacts, while agent_b is a conversational agent that may consume upstream outputs through REST, SDK, or MCP. If agent_b treats agent_a's outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing plans. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without independent validation
IF agent_a's generated text is used as source material for agent_b responses or actions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a output
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default
Limit agent_b to summarization rather than execution
Add checksum or schema validation on exchanged artifacts
requires-engineering: build a reviewer/arbiter stage

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while agent_a handles repository metadata, code, and task prompts. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and both are open-source with allowlisted egress. The only concrete compliance concern is a possible policy mismatch if sensitive user data is routed into agent_a's repo-oriented workflows.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from agent_b into agent_a's repository workflows
IF the deployment imposes retention or residency rules not enforced by either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_a inputs
Document retention for both agents
Review data-class routing before deployment
Restrict logs to minimal metadata
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
